newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures surge to end up by daily limit.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures surge to end up by daily limit.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed sharply higher on Monday with all contracts rising by their 400 yen daily limit as gains on the CBOT Project A overnight trading session triggered buying, traders said.
Benchmark July 1998 was up 400 yen at 13,600 yen per tonne at the close. Estimated volume was 57,346 lots.
"Gains on the CBOT overnight corn trading triggered buying from local investors," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.54-1/4 per bushel at 0800 GMT, against $2.51-1/2 at Friday's close.
Physical traders in Tokyo said that USDA's crop reports, released on Friday, was within their expectations and that there was no urgent need to buy U.S. corn immediately.
Spot July CBOT soybean was traded at $8.05 per bushel at 0800 GMT, against $7.85-1/2 at Friday's close.
